author: Astrokillah
text:
Hey man, good stuff there, I'm looking at the same thing! I like your
 level because it aligns with a very distinctive low to the left (See my
 thick orange line 1)

However, I must admit that since I went back to demo, trying to 'set and
 forget' my trades, the results had baaadddd! But ok, granted, I
looked at my losers, actually none of them fully meet the criteria I set
 out in my trading plan, I just took them because I was bored waiting
for valid setups.

RTM teaches us to find our trade at LTF levels. I normally look for kink in as low as 1 min.

For the LTF kink I want to trade, the criteria I set out are the following:

1. The kink must sit inside a HTF FL, and my HTF starts at H1 and above

2. The kink must align with a distinct LS or SR of HTF.

3. The HTF FL must have caused a valid engulf PA (with a clear TG not
reached). If not, I have to wait for engulf PA by the LTF kink I want to
 trade.

4. The approach back to the level of interest must have one of the following (compression, BSZ, 3Drive)

Oh well, as I'm finding out, setting rules are easy, but having the
patience to wait for the setup is another thing. And too often, the
setup occurred when I'm not in front of the PC!

So back to this USDCAD, it fulfills my rules #1 and #2, but not yet
fulfilled #3 and #4. So yes, I'm extremely eager to set PO there, but at
 the same time I'm hesitant!

What should I do???! Help!

AK

Full, your engulf there, is an engulf of a low, which is not what RTM
is teaching us. RTM says specifically that we need to engulf an FL.

It's not about who's right who's wrong, but we need to be clear about
who said what. I am struggling looking for valid engulf PA (even though
Bill in his previous post said he saw engulf PA all the time), but I beg
 to differ, a valid engulf PA (engulf of an FL with space to the next
FL) is a rare find.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Is it a matter of probability?

See this part of the chart (in red circle)

First, the blue zone is an important zone as you can see:

Now we zoom into the red circle:

Here, I have seen price engulfed south, breaking 3 demand levels before retracing up to FTR at point 4.

If we follow RTM's engulf rule, then this is not a valid engulf because
engulf of 3 is not enough, price hit and bounced upwards from the end of
 compression.

But if we follow an alternative rule - which is engulf of a low (or multiple engulf of low), then this would be a valid PA.
